name: Rabban Bar Sauma's embassy from the Ilkhanate to Europe
summary: Nestorian Christian monk of Uyghur origin, born in Khanbaliq (Beijing) c. 1220 and travelling west on pilgrimage from the 1270s, is dispatched by Ilkhan Arghun in 1287 to negotiate a Mongol-Christian alliance against the Mamluks. Visits Constantinople, Rome (interregnum), Genoa, Paris (where he meets Philip IV), Bordeaux (Edward I of England), and Rome again under Nicholas IV.

_quarry.structural_significance: First documented east-to-west embassy in the Latin Christian–Mongol diplomatic exchange; the reverse mirror of Plano Carpini and Rubruck. Bar Sauma's Syriac account survives in fragmentary form. The proposed Mongol-Christian alliance never materialised; the Mamluks decisively ended Mongol expansion into Syria at Wadi al-Khaznadar (1299) and Marj al-Saffar (1303).
